sections.title: Climbing shrub
sections.text: A prickly, scrambling rose native to China and recorded also in Laos and Vietnam. The Flora of China description gives stems 2–5 m long, leaflets mostly 2.5–6 cm long, and numerous white flowers about 2–2.5 cm across, borne in branched clusters. Its small, round red to dark-brown hips are 4–7 mm across.

sections.title: Name and comparison
sections.text: Taxonomic treatments disagree: Flora of China treats Rosa cymosa as a species, while Kew's current backbone places that name in synonymy under R. indica. The plate's white clustered flowers and small hips match the historical R. cymosa description. No species-specific human food or toxicity information was verified.
